smtp.title: Email / SMTP Settings
smtp.helpTip: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send invitation emails to new users. Without SMTP configuration, invitations cannot be sent automatically.
smtp.description: Configure SMTP to send invitation emails to users.

host.label: SMTP Host
host.help: Hostname of the outgoing SMTP server. Common examples: smtp.gmail.com (Gmail), smtp.office365.com (Microsoft 365), email-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com (Amazon SES). Ask your email provider for this value.

port.label: SMTP Port
port.help: TCP port of the SMTP server. Standard ports: 25 (SMTP without encryption, often blocked), 465 (SMTPS — SSL/TLS from connection), 587 (SMTP + STARTTLS — recommended for most modern servers). When in doubt, use 587.

username.label: Username
username.help: Login identifier for the SMTP server. For Gmail or Microsoft 365, this is typically your full email address. Some corporate SMTP servers use a separate identifier.

password.label: Password
password.help: SMTP password, stored encrypted on the server. For Gmail, use an App Password rather than your main account password. For Amazon SES, use the SMTP secret key generated in the AWS console.
password.revealPrompt: Enter your admin password to reveal the SMTP password.
password.hintMasked: Click "Show" to reveal with admin password.
password.hintUnchanged: If left unchanged, the existing password is kept on the server.

fromAddress.label: From Address
fromAddress.help: Email address displayed as the sender in invitation emails. Can include a display name, e.g. Calame <noreply@example.com>. This address must be authorized by your SMTP provider (verified domain on Amazon SES, alias in Gmail, etc.).

actions.saveTooltip: Saves the SMTP configuration on the server. Invitation emails will use these settings starting with the next invitation.
actions.testTooltip: Sends a test email to the "From" address to verify the SMTP connection works correctly before saving.

truncate.description: Masks part of the value, keeping only the configured number of leading and/or trailing characters.

exposeTunnel.heading: Remote access — Copilot & ChatGPT
exposeTunnel.headingHelp: Cloud AI platforms like Microsoft 365 Copilot and ChatGPT run in the cloud and can't reach a server on this machine directly. This opens a secure Cloudflare tunnel so they can connect to this MCP server over the public internet.
exposeTunnel.intro1: The public URL changes every time the tunnel restarts, and this machine needs to stay on and connected for it to keep working. Intended for evaluation — use a server deployment of Calame for production.
exposeTunnel.intro2: Privacy: your files and database never leave this machine — only the content of MCP requests and responses transits, encrypted, through Cloudflare's network (and every endpoint still requires your API token). For a setup where traffic terminates on your own infrastructure, use a server deployment. See docs/security-tunnel.md for the full threat model.
exposeTunnel.unavailable: Remote access is not available on this instance.
exposeTunnel.tokenNote: This endpoint still requires an API token — create one in the API Keys tab above.

copilot.step1: In Copilot Studio: Tools → Add a tool → New tool → Model Context Protocol.
copilot.step3: Authentication: API key. Location: Query. Parameter name: token.
copilot.step4: Paste your Calame API token (create one in the API Keys tab above), then Create.
copilot.step5: Add the new tool to your agent.

chatGpt.step1: In ChatGPT: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
chatGpt.step3: ChatGPT has no separate auth field here — it requires the token in the URL itself: append "?token='<'your token'>'" to the URL above.

guides.startTunnelHint: start the tunnel above to get this URL.
